blocks.text: In loot they show up named **MANUAL:** plus the gun (for example MANUAL: PPSH-41). They're random drops from military containers (green metal crates), weapons lockers, duffels in military areas, safes, locked key rooms and Irradiated Containers. Houses, gas stations and clinics won't have them.

blocks.text: **Season 1 guns.** Unlocking a gun on the Battle Pass gives you its Manual, so you can buy it at the Gunsmith: Cronen Osprey (assault rifle) at tier 16 and CSG-35 (SMG) at tier 36, both on the free track. The JAK 12 shotgun and ZLR Talonhawk axe come from a Season 1 event that hasn't been named yet. Buying a store bundle with a gun's blueprint also gives you that gun's Manual. A blueprint works in DMZ until you die with it, then you can rebuy it at a discount.

**BlackCell in DMZ:** each BlackCell blueprint unlocks its base gun at the Gunsmith; the FOB Vendor stocks an extra weapon and up to four pieces of Equipment; a daily reward at the DMZ Bunker (printer ingredients and the like) that doesn't stack, so claim it every 24 hours or lose it; and an Advanced Triage Kit survival kit when you buy it.

Only one M4 Manual find has been reported: a Tool Chest in the Prison Citadel yard. Owning an M4 blueprint also unlocks it at the Gunsmith: BlackCell gives the Perimeter Lance M4 the moment you buy it (the Vault Edition includes BlackCell), and the Valkyrie Mastercraft Bundle has the Skyfall M4. Put a Manual in a Secure Slot the moment you pick it up. The unlock only goes to the player who extracts it, and a Manual can be handed to a squadmate during the match, so pass it to whoever needs that gun before exfil.

blocks.text: **Bank caps.** Cash over the cap is thrown away. Start 100,000 · I 250,000 · II 500,000 · III 1M · IV 2M · V 5M · VI 10M · VII 25M · VIII 50M · IX 100M · X 250M · XI 500M · XII 1B · XIII 2B.
You pay per copy: base gun, each slot, then each attachment. Lose the gun and all of it goes with it, so most guns should come out of Hajin for free.

Suppressors and drum mags run about 9,500 to 15,000 each; the MEIKO 30CAL-SP at 9,500 is the cheapest suppressor. Discounts: 5% at DMZ Level 25 and 5% from Gunsmith I (stacking unconfirmed). Slots 3 to 5 come from guides other than DMZ Codex.

**Apex** is the attachment a gun unlocks at max weapon level. It changes how the gun works, doesn't use one of the five slots, and goes on free in DMZ. Weapon levels are shared with Multiplayer and Warzone.

blocks.text: Everything else in that Operator's loadout and backpack is lost too, and one report says Secure Slots don't protect anything, so stash keepers first. It's separate from your 1–70 DMZ level; FOB upgrades, recipes and Manuals stay unlocked. There's no DMZ-level prestige after 70.

**X01 (Season 1).** An underground GRANIT Arms black site under northwest Hajin, near the northern border. Hit the gate switch at the facility, then take the elevator with your whole squad inside it. No key or level needed. Exfils close as the match goes on, so you have to finish its steps inside to get out. Ghost is your Watcher inside, and it has its own Orders pages and its own 3D Printer. The X01 printer recipes are on the Crafting tab under X01 Printer (from one source). It also prints Experimental Compounds (2 Volatile Explosives + 5 Binding Catalyst) and Nano-Structured Alloy (2 Turned Components + 5 Structural Alloy).

**Season 1 Threat Briefings:** The Captain, a new Commander in X01; take pieces of his helmet, and more pieces mean better rewards, but only if you exfil with them. In Hajin, take parts off a North Korean battle tank, one per deployment; rewards grow with more parts across deployments.

**Also new in Season 1:** Resupply Run trades items from points of interest for Self-Revive Kits and 3-Plate Carriers (rates not published yet), and the FOB Vendor sells more weapons and gear for DMZ Cash, with extra stock for Season 1 BlackCell owners.

Upgrade costs, recipes and gun prices come from fan sites and community reports, re-checked Nov 7, 2026. Bank VIII–XIII match across two sources. Season 1 (Nov 5 patch notes) says FOB vendors, recipes and assembly requirements were updated but doesn't list the changes, so recipe and upgrade costs here are from before Season 1. When the printer or Gunsmith disagrees with this app, trust the game.
DMZ Codex was one of these sources. On Oct 30 its site started sending visitors to scam pages, so the app no longer links to it.
